title_en: Chen Yundou v. Laobianqiang Village Committee of Hushan Town, Kuandian Manchu Autonomous County — dispute over a mining rights transfer contract
ruling_gist_en: 1. The leasing of mining rights is a special form of transfer of mining rights. A contract for the transfer of mining rights is a contract that takes effect only after approval. According to the provisions of Article 10, Paragraph 3 of the Regulations on the Administration of Transfer of Exploration Rights and Mining Rights of the State Council, the leasing of mining rights must be approved by the competent authority with approval power. If the transfer is approved, the transfer contract takes effect from the date of approval.

full_text_en:
Chen Yundou v. Kuandian Manchu Autonomous County Hushan Town Laobianqiang Village Committee — Dispute over Mining Right Transfer Contract

【Ruling Summary】

1. The lease of mining rights is a special form of transfer of mining rights, and a mining right transfer contract is a contract that takes effect only after approval. Pursuant to Article 10, paragraph 3, of the Regulations on the Administration of Transfer of Exploration Rights and Mining Rights of the State Council, the lease of mining rights must be approved by the competent authority, and if the transfer is approved, the transfer contract takes effect from the date of approval.

2. During litigation, if a mining right lease contract has not been approved, the people's court shall find that the contract has not taken effect. Although the mining right contract has not taken effect, the provisions on application for approval agreed upon therein remain effective. If one party requests the other to continue performing the obligation to apply for approval, and the people's court, upon review, finds that objective conditions permit, its request shall be supported; if the continued application for approval lacks objective conditions, the request shall be rejected in accordance with law.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2011) Min Ti Zi No. 81

The complainant (plaintiff at first instance, appellant at second instance, applicant for retrial): Chen Yundou, male, Han ethnicity, born on August 9, 1952, residing at No. 4, Group 3, Laobianqiang Village, Hushan Town, Kuandian Manchu Autonomous County, Liaoning Province.

Agent ad litem: Qu Fengzhi, lawyer of Liaoning Mingge Law Firm.

The respondent (defendant at first instance, appellee at second instance, respondent to the retrial): Kuandian Manchu Autonomous County Hushan Town Laobianqiang Village Committee, domiciled at Laobianqiang Village, Hushan Town, Kuandian Manchu Autonomous County, Liaoning Province.

Legal representative: Liu Jiafa, director of the Village Committee.

Agent ad litem: Pan Ning, male, Han ethnicity, born on January 14, 1964, residing at No. 66-2-461, Ningzhong Road, Huanggu District, Shenyang City, Liaoning Province.

Agent ad litem: Cheng Shaowu, male, Han ethnicity, born on October 18, 1954, residing at Xijiabao Village Group, Tao Wai Village, Jiuliancheng Town, Zhen'an District, Dandong City, Liaoning Province, employee of Dandong Jiulong Group Co., Ltd.

In the dispute over a mining right transfer contract between Chen Yundou and Kuandian Manchu Autonomous County Hushan Town Laobianqiang Village Committee (hereinafter referred to as the Village Committee), Chen Yundou, dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2008) Liao Min Zai Zi No. 26 rendered by the Liaoning High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the Liaoning High Court) on August 14, 2009, filed a complaint with this Court. This Court, by civil ruling (2010) Min Jian Zi No. 2 dated December 15, 2010, decided to bring the case up for trial. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with law and held a hearing on April 1, 2011. The complainant Chen Yundou and his agent ad litem Qu Fengzhi, and the legal representative of the Village Committee Liu Jiafa and his agents ad litem Pan Ning and Cheng Shaowu appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The case has now been concluded.

On August 8, 2006, Chen Yundou filed a lawsuit with the Dandong Intermediate People's Court of Liaoning Province (hereinafter referred to as the Dandong Intermediate Court), alleging that on October 6, 2001, Chen Yundou, through lawful bidding, obtained the mining and operation rights for the First and Second Gold Mines of Laobianqiang owned by the Village Committee, and on the same day the parties signed the "Lease Agreement for Laobianqiang Gold Mine," stipulating that the mining and operation period was five years, from October 2001 to October 2006. After the contract was signed, because a third party, Cheng Shaowu, filed a lawsuit against the Village Committee, the Village Committee had not yet delivered the First Gold Mine of Laobianqiang (hereinafter referred to as the First Gold Mine) to Chen Yundou for operation. As for the Second Gold Mine of Laobianqiang (hereinafter referred to as the Second Gold Mine), because the Village Committee could not fully deliver the mining facilities, Chen Yundou had to invest additional funds to reopen the tunnel for mining. Moreover, due to disputes between the Village Committee and others, the mining license for the Second Gold Mine could not be obtained for three years, making performance of the contract impossible. Chen Yundou requested the court to: 1. order the Village Committee to perform the contractual obligation to deliver the First Gold Mine to him for operation; 2. if unable to deliver, substitute performance by the Second Gold Mine; 3. extend the contract period for the Second Gold Mine by three years; and 4. order the Village Committee to compensate him for economic losses of RMB 1.6 million.

In its defense at first instance, the Village Committee argued that Chen Yundou's claims had no factual or legal basis, that the Village Committee had no obligation to deliver the gold mine facilities to Chen Yundou, and that Chen Yundou's inability to obtain a mining license was unrelated to the Village Committee. Chen Yundou's claim for damages had no objective basis, and his losses should not be borne by the Village Committee.

The Dandong Intermediate Court, upon first instance trial, found the following facts: On August 31, 2001, the contract term of the original contractor of the Laobianqiang Gold Mine (divided into the First Gold Mine and the Second Gold Mine) with the Village Committee expired. On September 28 of the same year, the Village Committee published the "Lease Notice for Laobianqiang Gold Mine," the main content of which was: The contract for Laobianqiang Gold Mine expired on September 1, 2001. In accordance with the relevant provisions of the Mineral Resources Law and the spirit of Documents Nos. 34 and 35 of the County Government in 1999, and upon discussion and decision at the villagers' representative assembly, an open public tender is now conducted: the base price is RMB 400,000, plus an additional 20% of the total bid amount as town government management fees; the contract term is five years; all procedures for the gold mine shall be handled by the contractor at its own expense; the equipment, electricity, and ore on the stockpile belong to the original contractor, who must remove them within 20 days from the date of the bid; during the contract term, all legal liabilities and economic disputes arising from the mine shall be borne by the new contractor, and the Village Committee shall bear no economic responsibility.

On October 6, 2001, Chen Yundou (Party B) won the bid and signed the "Lease Agreement for Laobianqiang Gold Mine" with the Village Committee (Party A), stipulating that the Village Committee, through tender, leased the Laobianqiang Gold Mine to Chen Yundou for mining and operation, with a term of five years from October 2001 to October 2006. Chen Yundou shall pay the Village Committee a lump sum of economic compensation for five years and also pay a lump sum of 20% of the winning bid amount to the town government as compensation; all procedures for the gold mine shall be handled by the contractor at its own expense. If unable to mine due to failure to complete the relevant procedures, the rent shall not be refunded, and any losses incurred shall be borne by Chen Yundou. The equipment, electricity, ore on the stockpile, and ore mined by the original contractor in the mine shaft belong to the original contractor; during the lease term, all economic and legal liabilities arising from the mine shall be borne by Chen Yundou, and the Village Committee shall bear no responsibility. Upon expiration of the five-year term, the Village Committee and Chen Yundou shall negotiate a new agreement, but the compensation shall not be less than the current winning bid amount and the 20% of the winning bid amount paid to the town government. If Chen Yundou does not continue operation, the Village Committee shall reclaim the mining rights of the gold mine and conduct a tender; if Chen Yundou does not continue operation, he must remove the equipment within 20 days, otherwise the Village Committee has the right to forcibly remove it at Chen Yundou's expense, and the consequences shall be borne by Chen Yundou; if one party breaches the contract, it shall compensate the other party for direct economic losses and also pay liquidated damages of RMB 20,000. The parties also agreed on other matters.

After the agreement was signed, because Cheng Shaowu, the original contractor of the Laobianqiang Gold Mine, did not timely remove his equipment from the First Gold Mine, Chen Yundou could not operate the mine normally as agreed. Additionally, due to reasons attributable to Cheng Shaowu and his relatives, the Liaoning Provincial Department of Land and Resources only issued mining licenses for the Second Gold Mine for the years 2002 and 2005. Mining licenses for the Second Gold Mine for 2001, 2003, and 2004 were not processed or issued. Furthermore, it was found that during Chen Yundou's operation of the Laobianqiang Gold Mine, he added structures to the mine's underground tunnels. Appraisal determined that the value of the mine tunnel works added by Chen Yundou was RMB 706,874.90.

The Dandong Intermediate Court held at first instance that before signing the lease agreement, both Chen Yundou and the Village Committee knew that the original lessee of the mine, Cheng Shaowu, was detained for criminal offenses, the term of his lease had expired, but the mining license had not been returned to the Village Committee, and his mining equipment and some ore remained in the mine and had not been removed. The Village Committee disclosed the relevant circumstances in its notice. The Village Committee's approach was to circumvent commercial risks and protect its own interests, which did not violate legal provisions. Chen Yundou voluntarily accepted the conditions set by the Village Committee and participated in the bidding, and the parties' agreement in the contract regarding the relevant circumstances was also valid.

During performance of the agreement, the Village Committee assisted Chen Yundou to the best of its ability in excluding interference from third parties and handling the mining license, and neither Chen Yundou nor the Village Committee disputed this. Now Chen Yundou claims that during performance, due to interference from a third party, he could not exercise the five-year mining right and requests that the Village Committee extend the lease term as agreed, on the ground that the Village Committee should recover the already-leased gold mine from the third party, which is inconsistent with the terms of the lease agreement. The reason for Chen Yundou's inability to fully perform the lease agreement was the tortious conduct of a third party, and Chen Yundou should assert his rights against the tortfeasor. The Village Committee had no fault in the performance of the lease agreement and should not bear civil liability. Accordingly, on December 18, 2006, the court rendered civil judgment (2006) Dan Min San Chu Zi No. 52, dismissing Chen Yundou's claims.

Dissatisfied with the first instance judgment, Chen Yundou appealed to the Liaoning High Court on December 30, 2006, arguing that: (1) The first instance judgment misapplied the facts. It found that the reason for the incomplete performance of the lease agreement was the tortious conduct of a third party, and that Chen Yundou should seek relief from the tortfeasor, and that the Village Committee had no fault and should not bear civil liability. This finding was erroneous. The Village Committee's failure to perform the agreement was itself a breach of contract. In the "Lease Notice for Laobianqiang Gold Mine," the Village Committee stated: "Equipment, electricity, and ore on the stockpile belong to the original contractor, who must remove all equipment within 20 days from the date of the bid." Chen Yundou relied on this statement when he participated in the bidding and signed the lease agreement. As the holder of the mining rights, only the Village Committee could recover the mining license from the original contractor. The first instance judgment's finding that such risk should be borne by Chen Yundou was erroneous. (2) The first instance judgment's failure to apply the Contract Law of the PRC was erroneous. This case is a contract dispute. Article 121 of the Contract Law provides: "If a party breaches the contract due to a third party, it shall be liable to the other party for breach of contract, and the disputes between the party and the third party shall be resolved in accordance with law or the agreement." However, the first instance judgment found that Chen Yundou should assert rights against the third party. The lease agreement in this case is lawful and valid. Chen Yundou paid the corresponding amount of rent according to the winning bid and should enjoy the rights agreed in the contract. His appeal requests were: 1. to set aside the first instance judgment; 2. to order the Village Committee to perform the obligation to deliver the First Gold Mine to Chen Yundou for operation; if unable to deliver, substitute performance by the Second Gold Mine for five years; and 3. to order the Village Committee to compensate Chen Yundou for economic losses of RMB 706,874.90.

In its defense at the second instance trial, the Village Committee argued that according to the contract and the objective facts, the Village Committee had no breach of contract, it had already delivered the gold mine, and Chen Yundou's request for substitute performance by the Second Gold Mine if the First Gold Mine could not be delivered had no legal basis; regarding the failure to obtain a mining license, the agreement provided that Chen Yundou should handle it himself, and if mining was impossible, the loss was his own, and during performance Chen Yundou had indeed mined. Furthermore, according to Article 6 of the Regulations on the Administration of Civil Explosive Materials of the State Council, persons with criminal records are prohibited from engaging in the purchase of civil explosive materials and blasting operations. Chen Yundou had been sentenced for illegal logging and was thus legally disqualified from mining operations; his requests for extension of the contract term were unfounded. Since the Village Committee had no breach of contract, it should not bear compensation liability. The first instance court correctly found the facts, applied the law, and followed proper procedure, and the appellate court should dismiss the appeal and affirm the judgment.

The Liaoning High Court confirmed the facts found by the first instance court. No new evidence was submitted by the parties at the second instance.

The Liaoning High Court further found: On March 7, 2005, the first instance court rendered civil judgment (2003) Dan Min Yi He Chu Zi No. 117 in a related case, where the plaintiff was third party Cheng Shaowu, the defendants were Chen Yundou and the Village Committee, and the cause of action was a dispute over gold mine contract operation rights, property ownership, and property return. The court dismissed Cheng Shaowu's claims. After Cheng Shaowu appealed, the Liaoning High Court rendered civil judgment (2005) Liao Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 235 on October 11, 2005, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

The Liaoning High Court held at second instance that the lease agreement in question reflected the true intentions of both parties and was validly concluded. Regarding the acquisition and transfer of mining operation rights, relevant provisions of the Mineral Resources Law of the PRC and its implementing rules, the Regulations on the Administration of Transfer of Exploration Rights and Mining Rights of the State Council, and the Interim Provisions on the Administration of Transfer and Assignment of Mining Rights of the Ministry of Land and Resources clearly provide that mining operation rights are a type of franchise and their approval must strictly follow statutory procedures. The lease agreement in question did not undergo the mandatory approval procedures required by law, which falls under Article 52(5) of the Contract Law, and should be void.

A void agreement has no legal effect from the outset, and partial invalidity does not affect the validity of other parts. Chen Yundou's claim that the Village Committee breached the contract had no legal basis and was not accepted. Damages for losses arising from a void agreement should be considered based on the fault of the parties at the time of signing. However, given that Chen Yundou did not assert that the Village Committee should bear pre-contractual liability or provide relevant evidence in the first instance, his claim that the losses should be compensated lacked sufficient legal basis and was not supported. On July 30, 2007, the court rendered civil judgment (2007) Liao Min Er Zhong Zi No. 91, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

Dissatisfied with the second instance judgment, Chen Yundou applied for retrial to the Liaoning High Court, arguing that: (1) The second instance judgment misapplied the facts and the law. The second instance court erroneously characterized the lease relationship between Chen Yundou and the Village Committee as a contract for the transfer of mining rights through subcontracting, and its finding that the agreement did not undergo mandatory approval procedures lacked sufficient evidence and was factually erroneous. The second instance judgment's reliance on laws, regulations, and administrative regulations to find the agreement void was an error in the application of law. The Interim Provisions on the Administration of Transfer and Assignment of Mining Rights, one of the bases for the judgment, is an administrative regulation and cannot serve as a basis for finding an agreement void. Even if the parties failed to complete registration formalities, this should not affect the validity of the agreement, because the relevant laws and regulations neither require registration for mining lease agreements nor stipulate that registration is a condition for effectiveness. (2) The Village Committee's breach of contract caused Chen Yundou's failure to fully obtain the gold mine lease rights, and the Village Committee should bear liability for breach and compensate for the losses caused to Chen Yundou. Therefore, he requested: 1. to set aside the second instance judgment; 2. to amend the judgment to order the Village Committee to deliver the First Gold Mine to Chen Yundou as per the lease agreement; if unable to deliver, substitute performance by the Second Gold Mine for five years; extend the term of the Second Gold Mine agreement by three years; and 3. to order the Village Committee to compensate Chen Yundou for economic losses of RMB 1.6 million.

In its defense at retrial, the Village Committee argued that the original judgments were correct and should be affirmed.

On May 20, 2008, the Liaoning High Court rendered civil ruling (2007) Liao Li Min Jian Zi No. 489, ordering a retrial of the case.

At retrial, the Liaoning High Court found: On October 14, 2001, the Village Committee completed the "Registration Form for Application for Lease of Mining Rights," which stated a lease term of five years. The Kuandian Manchu Autonomous County Mining Office and Dandong City Planning and Land Resources Bureau indicated approval, but the Liaoning Provincial Department of Land and Resources did not approve. The copies of the "Business License" with validity dates ending April 30, 2004, and April 30, 2006, respectively, showed that Chen Yundou was the legal representative of the Second Gold Mine. On July 5, 2005, the Village Committee decided to remove Chen Yundou from that position and appointed Jiang Xinde as the legal representative of the mine.

The Liaoning High Court found no other facts different from those established at the second instance.

The Liaoning High Court held at retrial that the issue was whether the lease agreement was valid. Pursuant to Article 6 of the Mineral Resources Law and Article 3(2) of the Regulations on the Administration of Transfer of Exploration Rights and Mining Rights, unless there is a change in the ownership of enterprise assets such as merger, division, joint venture, or joint operation, and subject to lawful approval for the transfer of mining rights, the transfer of mining rights is not permitted. Article 36 of the Interim Provisions on the Administration of Transfer and Assignment of Mining Rights provides that the transfer of mining rights refers to the act of a mining rights holder transferring mining rights, including sale, contribution as capital, cooperation, restructuring, etc.; the lease and mortgage of mining rights shall be managed in accordance with the conditions and procedures for transfer of mining rights and require examination and approval by the original issuing authority. The above laws and regulations impose mandatory norms on the lease and other forms of transfer of mining rights. The lease of the mining rights for the gold mine in question must also satisfy the conditions set by the State Council and be managed in accordance with the conditions and procedures, subject to examination and approval by the original issuing authority. Although the "Registration Form for Application for Lease of Mining Rights" completed by Chen Yundou and the Village Committee in 2001 was approved by the Kuandian Manchu Autonomous County Mining Office and Dandong City Planning and Land Resources Bureau, this was a review opinion submitted by the lower-level mining authorities for approval as part of the administrative process and did not have the effect of an administrative permit. According to Article 11(2) of the Mineral Resources Law, municipal-level mining departments do not have approval authority. Before the Liaoning Provincial Department of Land and Resources rendered an administrative permit, it should be considered that the application was still pending and had not been approved by the competent approval authority. Therefore, the gold mine lease agreement in question was void for violating mandatory legal provisions.

Regarding whether the Village Committee breached the contract and should compensate Chen Yundou: Because the lease agreement was void, there was no basis for holding the Village Committee liable for breach of contract in accordance with the valid agreement. The consequence of voidness is that a right to claim restitution and damages arises between the parties. Throughout the first instance, second instance, and retrial proceedings, Chen Yundou sought liability for breach of contract but did not assert pre-contractual liability. Given that Chen Yundou neither claimed that the Village Committee should bear pre-contractual liability for damages nor provided evidence, his argument that he suffered losses due to the non-delivery of the First Gold Mine, requiring him to invest heavily in constructing new tunnel works, lacked sufficient legal basis and was not supported.

After discussion by the Judicial Committee of the Liaoning High Court, the court rendered civil judgment (2008) Liao Min Zai Zi No. 26 on August 14, 2009, affirming civil judgment (2007) Liao Min Er Zhong Zi No. 91.

Dissatisfied with the civil retrial judgment (2008) Liao Min Zai Zi No. 26, Chen Yundou filed a complaint with this Court on November 27, 2009, arguing that the relationship between him and the Village Committee was a lease contract relationship, the content of the lease contract did not violate mandatory legal provisions, and he fulfilled registration procedures in accordance with relevant regulations, and the Liaoning Provincial Department of Land and Resources had issued a mining license for him in 2002, so the retrial judgment's finding that the agreement was void was erroneous. Furthermore, in the case of Cheng Shaowu v. the Village Committee and Chen Yundou, the court had already found the lease agreement in question valid and accordingly dismissed Cheng Shaowu's claims. The retrial court's contradictory judgment on the same agreement was clearly erroneous. Therefore, he requested: 1. to set aside the civil judgment (2008) Liao Min Zai Zi No. 26 of the Liaoning High Court; and 2. to support Chen Yundou's claims.

Upon retrial, this Court finds: After the execution of the subject lease agreement, Chen Yundou paid a lump sum of compensation (i.e., rent) in the amount of RMB 540,000 in accordance with the agreement. On October 9, 2006, the Village Committee and Cheng Xianfeng entered into the "Kuandian County Hushan Town Laobianqiang Village No. 2 Gold Mine Mining Right Transfer Agreement." Thereafter, Cheng Xianfeng had the mining license for the mine transferred to his own name and became the holder of the mining right for the mine, with the validity period until March 7, 2012. The Village Committee is no longer the holder of the mining rights for the No. 1 Gold Mine and the No. 2 Gold Mine.

Other facts found by this Court are consistent with those found by the Liaoning High People's Court.

Opinion of the Court

This case concerns a dispute arising from the performance of the "Laobianqiang Gold Mine Lease Agreement" between the Village Committee as the lessor and Chen Yundou as the lessee. In this legal relationship, the Village Committee is the holder of the mining right, and the parties agreed to lease the mining right, not the entire mine including mining equipment. Leasing a mining right is a special form of transfer of a mining right and does not result in a change of the subject holding the mining right. Based on the nature of the civil legal relationship asserted by the parties in this case, the cause of action should be determined as a dispute over a mining right transfer contract. The original judgment's determination of the cause of action as a "dispute over the extension of the term of a mine lease contract and compensation" is inappropriate and should be amended.

Based on the facts found by this Court and the submissions and defenses of both parties, the focal issues in dispute between the parties in this case are: (1) Whether the subject "Laobianqiang Gold Mine Lease Agreement" is valid; (2) Whether the Village Committee has breached the contract and should bear liability for breach of contract, and whether the lease agreement should continue to be performed. These issues are analyzed separately as follows:

(1) Regarding the validity of the subject "Laobianqiang Gold Mine Lease Agreement."

Chen Yundou contends that the subject lease agreement is valid. His reasons are: 1. The subject gold mine previously had a mining license and had been contracted to another person; 2. The local county and municipal land and resources departments had approved the Village Committee's application for approval of the leasing of the mining right, but it was not completed due to the impact of another lawsuit; 3. In another similar lawsuit, the court found the mining right lease agreement to be valid. The Village Committee contends that the subject lease agreement was not approved by the Liaoning Provincial Department of Land and Resources and is therefore invalid. This Court holds that the mining industry is a licensed industry. According to relevant laws and administrative regulations, obtaining the mining right and the leasehold right for the subject gold mine both require approval from the Liaoning Provincial Department of Land and Resources. If either of these rights is not approved, the mining activities are not protected by law. Article 10, paragraph 3, of the State Council's "Measures for the Administration of the Transfer of Exploration Rights and Mining Rights" (February 12, 1998) provides: "Where the transfer is approved, the transfer contract shall take effect from the date of approval." Article 36, paragraph 2, of the Ministry of Land and Resources' "Interim Provisions on the Administration of the Transfer and Assignment of Mining Rights" (November 1, 2000) provides: "The leasing and mortgaging of mining rights shall be managed in accordance with the conditions and procedures for the transfer of mining rights, and shall be examined and approved by the original issuing authority." Accordingly, this Court finds that the subject lease agreement has been lawfully formed but has not yet taken effect. The terms of the agreement have no binding force on the parties, nor do they give rise to liability for breach of contract.

Both the subject "Laobianqiang Gold Mine Lease Notice" and the "Laobianqiang Gold Mine Lease Agreement" are constituent parts of the contract, with the latter serving as a confirmation and supplement to the former. Article 4 of both documents states: "All procedures for the gold mine shall be handled by the contractor at its own expense." The latter also provides: "If mining is impossible due to improper handling of relevant procedures, the rent shall not be refunded. Any losses incurred shall also be borne by Party B (i.e., Chen Yundou)." It can be seen from this that the obligation to handle all procedures for the gold mine as agreed was on Chen Yundou, and the responsibility for incomplete procedures also fell on Chen Yundou. At the time of signing the contract, Chen Yundou clearly knew that the Village Committee had not yet recovered the mining license from the original contractor, and that leasing the gold mine would involve enormous commercial risks. Nevertheless, he insisted on bidding and signing the above agreement, which was an act of assuming the risk. After the agreement was signed, the Village Committee actively handled the approval procedures for the lease of mining rights. The relevant competent departments of the local county and municipal governments had examined and approved the matter, but approval was not obtained from the Liaoning Provincial Department of Land and Resources solely because Cheng Shaowu refused to surrender the original mining license and sued the Village Committee. The Village Committee fulfilled its obligation of assistance in this regard and was not at fault. Accordingly, the Village Committee did not constitute a breach of contract for the incomplete mining right lease procedures and should not bear liability for breach of contract.

(2) Regarding whether the Village Committee breached the contract and should bear liability for breach of contract, and whether the lease agreement should continue to be performed.

Chen Yundou contends that the Village Committee failed to complete all mining licenses and deliver the subject gold mine, forcing him to reopen the tunnel, which constituted a breach of contract, and that the Village Committee should bear liability for breach of contract. The Village Committee contends that the subject lease agreement is invalid and does not give rise to liability for breach of contract. This Court holds that after the subject lease agreement was signed, the agreement was not fully performed for various reasons, resulting in Chen Yundou being unable to normally mine and indeed suffering economic losses. However, since the agreement has not taken effect and is not binding on the parties, the losses suffered by Chen Yundou cannot be remedied based on the breach of contract clauses of the agreement. Therefore, Chen Yundou's assertion that the Village Committee is responsible for the failure to perform the agreement and should bear liability for breach of contract is not supported. Leasing a mining right presupposes the lawful holding of the mining right. Given that the Village Committee is no longer the subject holding the mining right for the subject gold mine, it has lost the conditions and ability to perform. It is impossible for it to handle the relevant approval procedures as agreed and continue to perform the subject lease agreement. Accordingly, Chen Yundou's assertion that the subject lease agreement should continue to be performed is not supported by this Court.

Although Chen Yundou suffered economic losses from mining, his act of excavating the tunnel without authorization while clearly knowing that the lease agreement had not taken effect was an illegal mining operation. Such an act is not protected by law, and he shall bear the consequences. His claim that the Village Committee should compensate him RMB 1.6 million for breach of contract lacks legal basis and is not supported by this Court. Since the subject lease agreement has not taken effect, the rent received by the Village Committee from Chen Yundou should in principle be returned. However, given that Chen Yundou did not raise this claim in this case, this Court cannot directly order its return. Chen Yundou may seek resolution through other legal channels.

In summary, the subject mining right lease agreement has not taken effect, and the Village Committee should not bear liability for breach of contract. Alternatively, even if the lease agreement were deemed valid, since the agreement both provides that the Village Committee is exempt from liability, and that Chen Yundou shall bear the risks arising from the inability to mine and operate as agreed, the Village Committee equally should not bear liability for breach of contract. Given that the Village Committee is no longer the subject of the mining right, the subject lease agreement can no longer be performed. Chen Yundou's basis for claiming continued performance of the agreement is insufficient, and his claims are not supported. The judgment of the Liaoning High People's Court upon retrial found the basic facts clearly. Although there are flaws in finding the subject lease agreement invalid and in the cause of action, the result of the judgment is correct and should be affirmed. Pursuant to Article 186, paragraph 1, of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 37 of the Supreme People's Court's "Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China in the Trial Supervision Procedure," the judgment is as follows:

Affirm the Civil Judgment (2008) Liao Min Zai Zi No. 26 of the Liaoning High People's Court.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Han Mei

Trial Judge: Zhang Jinxian

Acting Trial Judge: Song Chunyu

November 30, 2011

Clerk: Han Shuai

[Introduction to the Presiding Judge]

Han Mei, senior judge: Born in 1962, Master of Laws. Served as a trial judge of the Supreme People's Court since 2000.
